question.prompt: Let \(M\) be the least common multiple of all the integers \(10\) through \(30,\) inclusive. Let \(N\) be the least common multiple of \(M,\) \(32,\) \(33,\) \(34,\) \(35,\) \(36,\) \(37,\) \(38,\) \(39,\) and \(40.\) What is the value of \(\dfrac{N}{M}?\)

solutions.title: Compare prime powers
solutions.explanation:
An LCM uses the greatest required power of each prime, so we can find what changes without calculating either large number.

For the integers from \(10\) through \(30\), the largest required powers of \(2,3,5\) are \(16,27,25\), respectively. The other required primes give
\[
M=2^4\cdot3^3\cdot5^2\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\cdot19\cdot23\cdot29.
\]
Here \(7\) is required, for example, by \(14\).

Of the additional numbers, \(32=2^5\) requires one more factor of \(2\), and \(37\) introduces a new prime. All the others already divide \(M\), as their factorizations show:
\[
\begin{aligned}
33&=3\cdot11,&34&=2\cdot17,&35&=5\cdot7,\\
36&=2^2\cdot3^2,&38&=2\cdot19,&39&=3\cdot13,\\
40&=2^3\cdot5.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the only necessary changes are multiplication by \(2\) and by \(37\). Therefore
\[
\frac{N}{M}=2\cdot37=\boxed{74},
\]
which is choice D.
